explain.title: The coordinate plane
explain.body: Draw two perpendicular number lines that meet at the origin O. The horizontal line x'Ox is called the x-axis and the vertical line y'Oy is called the y-axis. A point is named by an ordered pair (x, y).

explain.title: Coordinates and quadrants
explain.body: The first component of the ordered pair (x, y) is called x-coordinate or abscissa and the second component is called y-coordinate or ordinate of P. In Quadrant I both coordinates are positive; in II x is negative and y positive; in III both are negative; in IV x is positive and y negative. Points on the x-axis have the form (a, 0), and points on the y-axis have the form (0, b).

explain.title: Distance between two points
explain.body: For A(x₁, y₁) and B(x₂, y₂), the distance formula is d = √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²). Subtract matching coordinates, square the differences, add them, and take the square root. Distance is always non-negative.

explain.title: Midpoint of a line segment
explain.body: The midpoint is halfway between two endpoints. Average the x-coordinates to get its x-coordinate and average the y-coordinates to get its y-coordinate: M(x, y) = ((x₁ + x₂)/2, (y₁ + y₂)/2).

mistakes: Mixing up x and y when substituting coordinates into a formula.
Forgetting to square both coordinate differences in the distance formula.
Giving a negative distance instead of a non-negative length.
Adding the coordinates for a midpoint but forgetting to divide each sum by 2.
Leaving a radical unsimplified when it can be simplified.
In right-triangle questions, using the wrong side as the hypotenuse instead of the side opposite the stated right angle.

explain.title: Inclination and slope
explain.body: The textbook defines inclination this way: “The angle α (0° < α < 180°) is measured counterclockwise from positive x-axis to a non-horizontal straight line ℓ is called the inclination of ℓ.” The textbook also defines slope this way: “In analytical geometry, slope or gradient m of a non-vertical straight line with α as its inclination is defined by: m = tan α.” A horizontal line has slope zero; a vertical line has an undefined slope.

explain.title: Slope from two points
explain.body: For points P(x₁, y₁) and Q(x₂, y₂), use m = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁). Subtract the y-coordinates in the same order as the x-coordinates. The textbook states: “If slope of AB = slope of BC, then the points A, B and C are collinear.”

explain.title: Parallel and perpendicular lines
explain.body: Two lines are parallel when their slopes are equal. They are perpendicular when m₁m₂ = −1, so their slopes are negative reciprocals.

explain.title: Choose an equation form
explain.body: Use y = mx + c when the slope and y-intercept are known. Use y − y₁ = m(x − x₁) when a point and slope are known. Use x/a + y/b = 1 when the x- and y-intercepts are known. A horizontal line has equation y = a, and a vertical line has equation x = b.

explain.title: General equation
explain.body: The general equation of a straight line is ax + by + c = 0, where a and b are not simultaneously zero. Rearranging it to y = mx + c₁ reveals its slope when b is not zero.

mistakes: Reversing the subtraction order for only the numerator or only the denominator when calculating slope.

Stopping at a point-slope equation when the question or answer key expects a simplified general-form equation.

notes.answer: Use the distance formula d = √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²) and the midpoint formula M = ((x₁ + x₂)/2, (y₁ + y₂)/2).
notes.explanation: A point is written as an ordered pair (x, y): x tells how far to move horizontally, and y tells how far to move vertically. Use the distance formula to find the length between two points and the midpoint formula to find the point halfway between them.

notes.title: Coordinate Geometry in Real Life
notes.answer: The distance formula gives the straight-line distance, and averaging the coordinates gives the midpoint.
notes.explanation: Use the distance formula to find the straight-line distance between two points. To find the midpoint, average the two x-coordinates and average the two y-coordinates. For a rectangular boundary, find its side lengths and add them to get the perimeter.
